claims.text: Role in hypercalcemia: isotonic saline plus a loop diuretic ↑urinary Ca excretion;
claims.quote: Another treatment is increasing urinary calcium excretion by giving isotonic saline plus a loop diuretic.

claims.text: 1 to 2 L saline over 2 to 4 h first unless significant HF (nearly all are hypovolemic);
claims.quote: Initially, 1 to 2 L of saline is given over 2 to 4 hours unless significant heart failure is present because nearly all patients with significant hypercalcemia are hypovolemic.

claims.text: furosemide 20 to 40 mg IV every 2 to 4 h prn to keep urine output ~250 mL/h;
claims.quote: Furosemide 20 to 40 mg IV every 2 to 4 hours is given as needed to maintain a urine output of roughly 250 mL/hour (monitored hourly).
Care must be taken to avoid volume depletion.

claims.text: check K and Mg as often as every 4 h and replace IV prn.
claims.quote: Potassium and magnesium are monitored as often as every 4 hours during treatment and replaced IV as needed to avoid hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia.

claims.text: Interactions (all diuretics): lithium—⍉, diuretics cut its clearance and risk toxicity;
claims.quote: Lithium generally should not be given with diuretics because they reduce lithium’s renal clearance and add a high risk of lithium toxicity.

claims.text: NSAIDs can blunt the diuretic and antiHTN effect of loop, K-sparing and thiazide diuretics.
claims.quote: the administration of a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agent can reduce the diuretic, natriuretic, and antihypertensive effects of loop, potassium-sparing and thiazide diuretics

claims.text: OD: supportive—replace fluid and lyte losses;
claims.quote: Treatment of overdosage is supportive and consists of replacement of excessive fluid and electrolyte losses.

claims.text: check lytes, CO2 and BP often.
claims.quote: Serum electrolytes, carbon dioxide level and blood pressure should be determined frequently.
